newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU suspends planned wheat export tax, no new date.
newsitem.headline: EU suspends planned wheat export tax, no new date.

text.p: The European Commission has suspended plans to tax daily soft wheat grain and flour exports without setting a date for taking a decision on whether or not to introduce the tax, a European Commission official said on Wednesday.
Earlier it was reported that approval had been delayed after EU sources said that France opposed proposed taxes of 15 Ecus a tonne on exports of soft grain and 20 Ecus a tonne on wheat flour.
The proposal was expected to have been adopted unanimously on Wednesday by the 20 EU commissioners under a so-called written procedure.

"It's suspended, there's no new deadline," the official said. "It can be reopened but it's not sure. We don't know what will happen now." Exporters who have taken out a nil value export licence will be liable to tax if they have not customs-cleared their grain and flour exports before the tax is approved.

The move was aimed at saving supplies for EU domestic consumers and dampening prices. Concern over world crop prospects following frost in the United States and dry weather in Europe had driven prices some 20 percent above EU intervention levels.

The official said the EU's cereals management committee would discuss the question of an export tax at their next meeting on May 15, but a final decision would be up to the Commission. Meanwhile the Commission would continue to reject all requests for wheat export licences.
